title: The chain rule as gears turning gears
examples: What is the chain rule in simple words?
Why do you multiply in the chain rule?

explain.say: Look at these three gears. The big one is x. Turn it, and the middle gear u turns, which turns the little gear y. The chain rule answers one question: if you turn x, how fast does y turn? Watch the big gear first.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: gears. Look at the driver gear, the small gear and the third gear. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

explain.say: See the middle gear? It is half the size, so it spins twice as fast as x. In maths we say du by dx is 2: u changes 2 times as fast as x. Can you see it racing?

explain.say: Now the little gear y. It is half the size of u, so it spins twice as fast as u. So dy by du is 2. Here is a check-in: if x turns once, how many times does y turn?

explain.say: Four times! Two times two. That is the chain rule: dy by dx equals dy by du times du by dx. Rates in a chain multiply. Try y equals 3x, all squared: u is 3x, so du by dx is 3, and dy by du is 2u. Multiply: 6u, which is 18x.

explain.say: Well done! Whenever one thing drives another, which drives another, you multiply the rates. A bicycle's pedals, chain and wheel work the same way, and so does every formula with a function inside a function.

faq.a: The chain rule tells you the rate of change of a function inside a function. You multiply the rate of the outer part by the rate of the inner part.
asks: What does the chain rule do?

faq.q: Why do you multiply in the chain rule?
faq.a: Because rates pass along the chain. If u changes 2 times as fast as x, and y changes 2 times as fast as u, then y changes 2 times 2, that is 4 times, as fast as x.
asks: Why is the chain rule a product?

faq.q: What is an inner and outer function?
faq.a: In y equals (3x) squared, the inner function is u equals 3x and the outer one is y equals u squared. You do the inner one first, then the outer one.
asks: How do I spot the inner function?

faq.a: Let u be 3x, so du by dx is 3. Then y is u squared, so dy by du is 2u. Multiply: 2u times 3 is 6u, which is 18x. Check: 9x squared also gives 18x.

faq.q: When do I use the chain rule?
faq.a: Use it whenever there is a function inside another function, like sine of 2x, e to the x squared, or a bracket raised to a power.
asks: How do I know when to use the chain rule?

facts: The chain rule states dy/dx = dy/du × du/dx.
The derivative of (3x)² is 18x, matching the derivative of 9x².

quiz.say: u changes 3 times as fast as x, and y changes 5 times as fast as u. How fast does y change compared with x?
quiz.show: u changes 3 times as fast as x, and y changes 5 times as fast as u. How fast does y change compared with x?

wrong.0: Adding the rates is the common slip; the chain rule multiplies.
wrong.1: Subtracting the rates does not follow the chain.

quiz.say: What is the derivative of 2x, all squared?
quiz.why: u = 2x gives du/dx = 2; y = u² gives dy/du = 2u. So 2u × 2 = 4u = 8x.

wrong.1: 4x forgets to multiply by the inner rate, 2.
wrong.2: 2x is far too small: (2x)² is 4x², whose derivative is 8x.
